title: Delta inventory: signal origins and triage cookbook
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a working notebook for mapping where a performance delta actually originates (hardware, kernel/runtime, model variant, routing policy, customer payload shape). Focused on the common case: small-but-actionable latency regressions that trigger 95th/99th percentile alerts in the hosted fleet or during canary windows. Aim: reduce investigator time-to-evidence and give a repeatable bisect path that teams can run without heavy orchestration.

High-level signal-origins approach (one-line summary)
- Assemble a tight slice of production traffic that reproduces the delta.
- Correlate metric deltas across layers (route -> model -> instance -> gpu driver -> kernel).
- Narrow to smallest change set using gated synthetic runs + git/artifact bisect.
- Validate with canary-vs-control comparisons and targeted profiling.

1) Initial triage checklist (first 15–30 minutes)
- Capture alert context: which dashboard, metric, time window, alert threshold and who paged. Record the exact query and window.
- Snapshot the canary and baseline commit hashes / model artifact ids involved.
- Quick segment: split the alert group by model_id, route, region, customer_tier, seq_length_bucket (0-64, 65-256, 257-1024).
- Check resource saturation: GPU util, mem alloc, CPU steal, host load, network transmit. Note if any host-level OOM/evictions.
- Scan for recent infra changes: driver upgrades, CUDA/cuDNN, kernel patches, instance family changes, autoscaling changes.
- Post initial findings into incident thread with a short hypothesis (e.g., "95th spike correlated with model=llama-13b-8bit and region=eu-west-1 starting 03:12 UTC").

2) Dashboard queries / examples (PromQL-like pseudocode for reproducibility)
- Baseline 95th latency for route X: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_bucket{route="/generate"}[5m])) by (le, route, model))
- Token-normalized latency per model: sum(rate(token_processing_time_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(token_processed_count[5m])) by (model)
- Percent deviation vs baseline (stored baseline series name BL): (current - BL)/BL * 100 — store as scripted alert to detect drift > 10% for 95th or > 20% for 99th depending on SLO.
- Compare canary vs control (split by rollout tag): avg_over_time(latency_ms{rollout="canary"}[5m]) / avg_over_time(latency_ms{rollout="control"}[5m])

3) Reproduction harness and synthetic traces
- Goal: isolate software changes from noisy production by replaying real traces through a controllable harness.
- Steps:
  1. Export a 30–60 minute sample of production requests for the offending route (anonymize PII). Save as replay/<incident>-trace.json. Include request size, seq length, model version, headers.
  2. Run replay against both baseline and candidate binaries/artifacts on identical instance types. Use pinned seeds and identical runtime configs (batching thresholds, KV cache evictions, quantization flags).
  3. Use a small fanout (N=1–4) to reduce variability, then scale to N=16–32 for throughput-affected deltas.
  4. Collect the same telemetry that production emits: latency percentiles, per-token timing, GPU kernel times, kernel-launch counts.

Commands / harness hints (pseudo)
- replay tool: ./tools/replay --trace replay/2025-11-02-llama13b.json --target http://localhost:8080/generate --concurrency 8 --seed 42 --collect=pprof,nvtx
- start runner: ./bin/runtime-server --model-path=/artifacts/model_v123 --batch-threshold-ms=8 --quant-mode=8bit
- capture perf (host): sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60; sudo perf script > perf.out
- capture pprof (runtime): curl http://localhost:9090/debug/pprof/profile?sec=30 > profile.pb.gz

4) Automated git/artifact bisect procedure
- Principle: make the smallest isolation step a single change (commit or artifact). If too many commits between baseline and candidate, do binary search using synthetic harness.
- Steps:
  1. Identify base artifact A (known-good) and candidate B (suspected).
  2. If commits are many, create mid-point M (build at mid-hash). Deploy M to harness and run the replay suite. Measure delta metric.
  3. Continue bisect until you find a commit/PR that flips the regression on or off.
  4. When commit found, check PR diff for runtime config changes, kernel tweaks, third-party dependency updates (protobuf, thriftruntime, jemalloc).

Pitfalls and noise controls
- Avoid changing instance types between runs. Differences in GPU microcode, driver versions, or CPU turbos can be noisy.
- Force deterministic random seeds where possible (sampling, top-k sampling, non-deterministic kernels).
- Account for cold-start variance: pre-warm models and measure only steady-state windows.
- When comparing canary vs control, compute both absolute and relative percentiles and look at the distribution tail shape (not just p95).

5) Canary vs control comparison recipe (quick cookbook)
- When running a canary that shows a delta: always run a parallel control cohort for the same trace. Collect per-request annotation: rollout_tag, model_commit, instance_id, sequence_length.
- Compute for each cohort: p50, p95, p99, tokens/sec, kernel-times breakdown. Visualize delta heatmap by sequence_length_bucket x percentile.
- Use statistical tests for significance (Mann-Whitney U for latency samples, KS-test for distribution shape) before escalating to rollback.

6) Profiling checklist (what to capture)
- Runtime stack traces (pprof) across the affected window. Look for new hotspots compared to baseline.
- GPU kernel durations (nvprof/nsight) and counts: increased kernel launches or higher average kernel time can indicate changed token paths or attention optimizations being disabled.
- NVTX ranges to correlate high-level phases (tokenization, encode, attention, decode).
- Memory allocator metrics: fragmentation, peak resident size, page faults; jemalloc changes occasionally alter tail latency.
- Tracing (opentelemetry): distributed spans for request -> model shard -> kernel to ensure no cross-service amplification.

7) Example mini-case (fictional but realistic)
- Symptom: 95th latency for /generate jump +18% starting 2025-10-28 04:10 UTC. Canary rollout of runtime v2.11.3.
- Quick triage: delta concentrated on sequences >256 tokens and model=redwood/llama-13b-q4. GPU util unchanged, but average kernel launch count increased by 14% for decode kernels.
- Replay: run 10k requests from trace against v2.11.1 (control) and v2.11.3 (candidate). Candidate shows the same +17% p95.
- Bisect: bisect identified PR #546 that changed attention tiling heuristic to a larger tile size on sequences >128. Reverting PR eliminated the spike.
- Root cause hypothesis: new tiling interacts badly with q4 quantized kernel causing additional small kernels to be launched per output token. Fix: restore previous tiling for q4 or add a condition to use legacy kernel for quantized path.

8) Postmortem and follow-up actions (quick template)
- Summary (1–2 sentences): what happened, impact, fix applied.
- Timeline: detection -> triage -> bisect -> fix -> rollout -> monitor. Include exact commits/artefacts.
- Root cause analysis: what change caused it and why did it affect tail latency specifically.
- Metrics blinded by fix: show before/after p95/p99 and token-normalized latency.
- Action items: code change, e2e test, dashboard alert tuning, post-deploy replay smoke. Assign owners and deadlines.

9) Future improvements (ideas to reduce time-to-evidence)
- Canary diff automation: on canary failure, automatically spin up a replay job that runs a canonical trace against baseline and canary and produces a delta report.
- Regression fingerprint index: store lightweight fingerprints (p95 by seq bucket, kernel counts) for every build to enable quick nearest-neighbor matching of incidents to prior regressions.
- Synthetic smoke suite for every runtime/driver combo (ci-matrix) that runs a minimal tokenized workload across seq-length buckets and reports regressions before a canary.

Notes, open questions and todo
- Need a standardized trace export format (include runtime annotations and token boundaries).
- Investigate building a tiny bisect runner that integrates with CI and the replay harness to automate binary searches across releases.
- Decide on alert thresholds per model family (some large-models have noisier tails and need higher thresholds).

Appendix: quick checklist card (one-liner actions)
- Capture alert metadata & post to thread.
- Tag and export trace sample (30–60m).
- Run replay against baseline & candidate.
- If reproducible, bisect commits/artifacts.
- Profile candidate & baseline, compare hotspots and kernel stats.
- If commit found, draft rollback or targeted fix + tests.
- Follow through with postmortem and dashboard tuning.

End of notebook — this is intentionally a portable working doc. Add run logs, perf artifacts and repro traces in the incident folder when available.
